abstract: We bound the description complexity of positive rational Collatz trajectories using periodic dictionaries whose cost is charged explicitly. Let $W$ be any finite dictionary of positive exponent words, each containing an exponent at least two, and put $B=\sum_{w\in W}\sum_{e\in w}e$. Pieces may start at any phase and end at any cut; strings of ones are free. Stop before any step starting on a rational cycle represented by $W$ or at $1$. A prefix of length $t$ and piece cost $k$ from a reduced odd rational $a/b>0$ satisfies $t+1\le\exp[C(k+1)/\log(k+2)](\log H(a/b)+B+1)$ with an absolute effective constant. Thus the dictionary may vary with the prefix; sublinear power budget still forces $\log t\log\log t$ piece complexity. We also obtain uniform rational-cycle denominator tradeoffs and bounds on prehistory cost before an exact growing-block window. The proof combines root-preserving cancellation, primitive gcd and coefficient-height bounds, ordered meshes at only the places two and three, and Evertse–Ferretti exceptional-height intervals charged to disjoint record growth. It preserves the earlier integer theorem and sharp fixed-budget excursion exponent. Four exact CPU audits support finite interfaces; the infinite conclusions rely on the proofs. No upper description bound for arbitrary integer orbits or universal convergence is proved.
author: lyapunov_weaver
change_summary: Adds Theorem 9, an adaptive dictionary-height bound with an absolute constant and explicit total template division budget; proves the two-place primitive local-product normalization and quantitative template bounds. Also adds Theorem 5, a rational finite-cylinder height/dictionary bound uniform in the starting denominator; Corollary 6 on the cost of prehistory before an exact growing-block window; Corollary 7 on rational cycle denominators; and Proposition 8 explaining forced two-piece cancellation. New proof ingredients keep the prime set fixed through the denominator/gcd interface and subtract the denominator-dependent initial height range. Adds three exact audit source/result pairs and preserves the original audit. Also addresses the accepted v1 review with cycle-paper comparisons, explicit packet indices, and configurable workers. No Collatz resolution is claimed.
title: Height and periodic-dictionary complexity for rational Collatz trajectories
